# Current owner direction: Ecosystem Sciences demonstration

Version: `2026-10-13.4`. Owner: Bryce / TokenJunkieLabs. Direction for the Upper Savannah application, demonstration, presentation and work orders. Continue the broad build and finish as much of the existing Eco science application as possible before Bryce's call. Bryce renewed this work directly at **October 13, 2026, 10:46 a.m. Eastern / 14:46 UTC**, after the earlier 10 a.m. preservation checkpoint. Resume the existing unfinished work from its actual saved state and preserve completed outputs, active processes and original implementation ownership.

## Direct owner instructions

Latest direct instruction, October 13 at 10:46 a.m. Eastern:

> Get as much of eco science done with the fleet as possible before my call. Try to get it finished its possible im throwing shit ton of agents just get it done

This current instruction supersedes the earlier 10 a.m. Eco work cutoff. Prior cutoff records remain historical evidence. Coordinate at the existing Eco thread, reconcile actual issued handles, complete unfinished integration and native receiving, and publish usable durable handoffs in the existing application. Preserve the distinction between the sender's completed runs and the runs actually included in a received Study. Existing workers keep their current operations; additional workers clear complementary blockers. The recorded call remains unchanged; this direction schedules no meeting or automation and authorizes no client message.

> do the simulated model

> just make sure that what we put infront of him is something he would need and want and he will be blown away how relevant it is to him and how he wants it,a nd also the speed we produced it

> just checking dont pause anythi g

> and make sure wherever the fleet is coordinating in slack or github or wherever on this demo / presentation / ecosystem gets that update toand passes it along to other agents because the feed may be moving fast

## Build for an experienced scientific practice

Ecosystem Sciences lists GIS, hydrology/monitoring, ecological modeling, watershed assessment, statistics, visualization, optimization and publishing. Tim Maguire's practice includes GIS, modeling and water resources. Its South Platte work assembled data, mapped natural capital and produced watershed investment decision support. Do not assume it lacks these capabilities. Its unmet tooling, InVEST or production-capacity gap is unknown until the call. Sources: [Services](https://www.ecosystemsciences.com/read-me), [Firm](https://www.ecosystemsciences.com/firm), [South Platte](https://www.ecosystemsciences.com/).

Show concrete delivery and engineering offload on the actual Upper Savannah RFP workflow: source assembly, reproducible native calculations, editable scenarios, useful decisions and a complete working handoff. The prime retains scientific direction, method choices, interpretation/review and the client relationship. Relevance comes from useful work they can inspect, adapt and receive; do not promise Tim's reaction or claim an unconfirmed need.

## Execute the prepared simulated case now

Native execution is the immediate hard priority. Issue the prepared simulated case on the verified scientific runtime, retain its actual run identity and progress, and obtain the real native outputs. Continue the source/runtime/application integration needed to make that happen. Further plans, stock demonstrations, policy reviews and cosmetic inspection do not replace execution. Do not introduce a bid decision or a prime's yes as a gate.

Demonstrate the scientific operation in the actual application:

1. Use the RFP's 30 m GIS selection. Keep the upstream contributing model domain distinct from the South Carolina reporting mask and the four existing utility focus anchors; retain their actual source geometries and identities.
2. Run the baseline, a realistic riparian alternative and its matched control with explicit, editable source editions, assumptions, parameters and scenario changes.
3. Show active run/progress/logs and completed native annual NDR/SDR results: nitrogen and phosphorus in **kg/year**, sediment in **tonnes/year**, representing delivery to streams. Do not present these modeled stream loads as intake concentrations.
4. Compare the actual maps, tables and report, preserving matched scientific support and original units. Keep source/assumption edits and their consequences inspectable.
5. Export the editable GIS/project and complete scientific working package. Cold-reopen the delivered application/project and show the retained sources, selections, results and useful controls.

Identify the simulated case as modeled. Never invent measurements, completion or customer acceptance.

## Present the real work and real speed

Actually open, see and use the outgoing app and every attachment as its recipient would. Repair defects and ship a plain, readable product. Apply the standing inspection rule without review/test theatre or parallel bureaucracy.

If producing video, record the actual working application and use available natural generative voice/TTS. Watch and listen to the final export. Generated frames must never pretend to be a working app. Explain speed using actual elapsed start, commit, run and package history; do not invent delivery times or guaranteed reactions.

## Carry this direction with the work

Pass this complete brief into every current child, provider and cloud work order and handoff. Include its durable path and version `2026-10-13.4` with the next result. Relay it at the actual coordination surface and onward to participating workers; fast feeds can bury an update. Acknowledgment alone is not delivery.

Preserve active compute and existing implementation ownership. Do not force worker restarts, drop an active run or create a new controller. Keep lab attribution, source/copyright, incident and contact controls, personal-meeting approval, no private GitHub/Actions, no llama.cpp and focused internal validation. No new approval gate or broad test sweep is authorized.

# Bind original measurements to an editable native Chemistry case

This workflow joins the existing Measurements source collection, record review and source revision engine to the original Chemistry 0.3 inference and transfer workflow. It retains the complete selected population, exact source rows and original measurement workspace alongside each prepared binding. The existing Chemistry queue performs numerical work.

## Open, review and prepare

Open **Measured observations**, choose an existing original Chemistry case, and inspect the actual imported measurement population. The inspector returns complete records, source links, review history, original spatial assignment and exclusion reasons, grouped by exact characteristic, analytical method, fraction, source basis and normalized unit.

A usable binding requires these explicit choices:

- The original station and actual selected case reach, with a source reference and assignment rationale. Existing HUC assignments are retained as context; they are not silently reused as chemical reaches.
- The exact original characteristic/method/fraction and its measured identity. Ammonia-N, nitrate-plus-nitrite-N and Kjeldahl-N are separate review choices.
- The conserved basis and its source evidence. A blank or unspecified source basis requires the analyst's explicit basis reference and rationale. A conflicting declared source basis is rejected.
- All modeled components and positive weights needed to represent the measured quantity. Components must share the selected conserved basis. A total-nitrogen label alone does not turn an ammonium-plus-nitrate model into a complete TKN-plus-NOx measurement.
- The original model time origin with time zone, or an explicit reviewed model day for a selected source record. Original dates and times remain retained. Samples outside the actual case duration remain excluded.
- An explicit positive uncertainty in mg/L with its rationale, and fit/holdout roles. A dated holdout boundary is supported; source records are never silently assigned a laboratory uncertainty.

The binding keeps quality-control exclusions, source-version conflicts, rejected reviews and unresolved native-domain changes. Only a specific reviewed interpretation resolves an unmapped constituent, a separate explicit chemical-reach assignment, or valid censored bounds.

### Censoring and original nutrient composition

The adapter reuses the existing exact-decimal Eighteenmile source reader in observations/eighteenmile_stoichiometry_20261013/stoichiometry.py. Its original published methods, unfiltered fraction, final status and strict below-quantification condition produce the original finite interval and open endpoint. Original source rows and rationales remain attached. Other sources need finite original bounds and an explicit endpoint review.

An interval uses qualifier interval, lower_mg_l, upper_mg_l, lower_closed and upper_closed. It has no substituted mg_l point value. An optional original TKN-plus-NOx selection uses the same STOICH concentration and plus functions, matches the original activity, station, time zone, sampling depth, medium and project, and retains both original row identities. The target nitrogen operator must exactly equal the disjoint weighted union of the selected original TKN and NOx modeled operators on basis N. Overlapping component pools, omitted pools and changed target weights remain excluded with explicit reasons. Ammonia is already part of TKN and is not added again.

When a TKN-plus-NOx target is created, its two component targets are removed from that request's independent observation population. Their source records and component interpretations remain retained. This prevents treating a derived sum and its same two measurements as three independent observations.

## Exact API

POST /api/measurements/chemistry is handled inside the original authenticated extension. Every body contains the existing workspace key and an action.

- catalog: original cases, saved bindings, explicit measurement choices and measurement_revision.
- inspect: case_id, filters and optional expected_revision. Returns case, revision, filters, complete records, source groups and measurement_choices.
- prepare: selection, with the structure below. Returns binding_id, the editable child case_id, original_case_id, counts, accepted/excluded populations, retained source and native_payload.
- get or export: binding_id. Export returns document, filename, content_type, sha256 and the original native Chemistry export action.
- adopt-source: case_id, source_collection_id and source_id. Reopens the complete binding document retained by an independently received original Chemistry case.

The selection uses actual original IDs. The following is a schema example; field values must come from the selected sources and native project:

~~~json
{
  "case_id": "ACTUAL_ORIGINAL_CASE_ID",
  "title": "Reviewed native observation selection",
  "reviewer": "ACTUAL_REVIEWER",
  "reason": "Scientific purpose and scope of this original source binding",
  "filters": {"stationId": "ORIGINAL_STATION", "from": "YYYY-MM-DD", "to": "YYYY-MM-DD"},
  "expected_revision": 1,
  "station_bindings": [
    {"station_id": "ORIGINAL_STATION", "reach_id": "ACTUAL_CASE_REACH",
     "reference": "Original spatial/source reference", "reason": "Assignment rationale"}
  ],
  "measurement_mappings": [
    {"characteristic": "EXACT ORIGINAL CHARACTERISTIC",
     "method": "EXACT ORIGINAL METHOD", "fraction": "EXACT ORIGINAL FRACTION",
     "measurement": "nitrate_nitrite_n", "basis": "N",
     "basis_reference": "Original method/basis source",
     "basis_reason": "How the selected modeled pools represent the measured quantity",
     "components": [{"species": "ACTUAL_CASE_SPECIES", "weight": 1}],
     "sigma_mg_l": 0.1, "uncertainty_reason": "Explicit reviewed uncertainty source"}
  ],
  "time_origin": "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+00:00",
  "day_overrides": {},
  "roles": {"default": "fit", "holdout_from": "YYYY-MM-DD", "by_record": {}},
  "allow_censored": true,
  "interval_overrides": {},
  "request": {"mode": "calibrate", "parameters": []}
}
~~~

The 0.1 uncertainty above illustrates JSON syntax; the application requires an actual reviewed value. Exact blank method/fraction strings may be selected when those are the original source fields.

day_overrides maps an exact record ID to {day, reason}. interval_overrides maps an exact record ID to {lower_mg_l, upper_mg_l, lower_closed, upper_closed, reason}; the bounds must agree with the declared source. It can explicitly review the physical zero lower bound of a left-censored concentration. It cannot invent a finite upper bound for an originally unbounded result.

Optional derived_total_nitrogen contains measurement: total_nitrogen, basis: N, basis_reference, basis_reason, components, sigma_mg_l and uncertainty_reason. It applies only to the exact supported original TKN and NOx methods at matching original sampling activities.

Native modes are calibrate, sensitivity, uncertainty and monitoring. The request contains that original mode's parameters, draws, count and other native settings. The binding supplies observations, so a competing request.observations is rejected.

## Original native operation and recovery

Preparation reads the original measured revision, every selected full record and the complete portable source in one SQLite read transaction through the existing Measurements process. An explicitly expected stale revision returns a conflict before source publication. A content-addressed identity, native file lock and immutable receiving receipt preserve the same selected operation across interruption. The first complete original portable snapshot is retained when a retry changes only its descriptive creation clock.

The source document and complete editable measurement snapshot enter the existing Workspace.import_sources intake. The new native Chemistry case is a child of the actual selected case, with the same physical project and both original and measured source references. Existing source cases remain available.

The returned native_payload has the original shape {case_id, request}. Run it through the existing chemistry.run operator action. Request metadata carries the complete selected interpretation, accepted/excluded populations, source IDs and original case identity. Numerical inference remains in the original engine.

The CLI uses the same actual managed Measurements service:

~~~sh
python -m measurement_workspace.chemistry --workspace ACTUAL_WORKSPACE \
  --output OUTSIDE_WORKSPACE/inspection.json inspect \
  --case-id ACTUAL_CASE --filters ORIGINAL_FILTERS.json

python -m measurement_workspace.chemistry --workspace ACTUAL_WORKSPACE \
  --output OUTSIDE_WORKSPACE/binding.json prepare --selection REVIEWED_SELECTION.json
~~~

The prepared native case and its completed analyses can be exported with the existing chemistry.export action and independently received through chemistry.receive. The source document and full measured snapshot travel as original native source bodies and companions. A complete Workspace transfer additionally retains the binding desk records directly.

For a selected Chemistry transfer, adopt-source reopens the binding already carried by the received case's exact source selection. Original sender IDs remain in received_from. The original Measurements receive operation can reopen the companion measurements.json into an explicitly chosen empty measured workspace before further record review; its original domain binder retains the receiver's explicit native source choice.

## Source composition and rendered inspection

This component adds measurement_workspace/chemistry.py and its source fragment, joins the current MeasuredObservationExtension and descriptor, and uses the existing browser helper. Source normalization, streaming intake, Published Studies and global operator files retain their existing owners.

Apply the repository's AGENTS.md requirement to the actual outgoing interface and scientific files: open and look at populated desktop/narrow views, operate inspection, preparation, case opening, native run, complete export and reopening, and repair visible defects. Source review alone does not establish the delivered product's rendered behavior.

## Complete original collection companions

When selected records belong to one or more retained Measurements collections,
preparation resolves their original import IDs against those collections' native
manifests. It uses the existing collection publisher and bundle exporter to
preserve each complete immutable edition ZIP. The ZIP contains every original
source and binary companion, the original collection manifest, the portable
measurement project, native domain identifiers and the original reports.

The edition must have the same source revision and complete portable project as
the reviewed atomic snapshot; only the descriptive creation clock may differ.
The exported native domain must also equal the inspected domain. A concurrent
record review or domain change requires a fresh inspection. ZIP byte identities,
embedded project/manifest identities and the complete member inventory are
checked before the unchanged ZIP becomes a companion of the binding's native
Workspace source.

### Native reach or HUC source binding

Open **Bind an original native reach or HUC source** above the desk. Choose a JSON/GeoJSON already retained within the original Workspace, its list field path and string identifier field path. ## Operator workflow

1. Receive a complete WQP/WQX3 chemistry CSV, stations CSV, or USGS OGC daily mean discharge GeoJSON. Alternatively retrieve a station/date range from the public providers. Inspect parse counts, rejected rows, units, fractions, censoring, mapping and source checksum, then commit the complete source.
2. Assign stations to the actual selected native identifiers. Filter measurements, open an exact record, inspect raw fields and every original source-row link, review qualified results, and select between conflicting revisions without deleting alternatives.
3. Export all measurements or the reviewed input population. The input package includes complete accepted/excluded records with reasons; no nondetect substitution or replicate averaging is performed. Create an optional explicit concentration/discharge pairing report with the actual station pairing and written rationale.
4. Export the complete editable measurement workspace. Receive it into an empty measurement workspace, reparse the original files, verify every canonical record and source link, and continue independent edits. Existing work is never overwritten.

The complete handover contains original source texts, original provider response pages, parse accounting and rejected rows, canonical measurements, station metadata, assignments, reviews, alternative revisions, events and saved exports. It is a portable JSON artifact, not a pointer to the sender's SQLite database. Native-domain source files remain owned by the original Workspace; bind the same retained source edition in the recipient's native app.

## Scientific semantics

Original strings are retained verbatim. Recognized mass concentration units normalize to mg/L without changing chemical basis; mg/L as N is not silently changed to mg/L as nitrate. Total/unfiltered nitrogen and phosphorus are distinct from dissolved or unspecified fractions. Nitrate and orthophosphate retain basis and fraction. BOD5 and carbonaceous BOD5 remain distinct, with no conversion to ultimate BOD. Blank values never become zero. Nondetects retain a null point value and an explicit lower/upper bound where the original result or one compatible detection limit supplies it. Multiple laboratory detection/quantitation limits are preserved rather than selected automatically.

Explicit time zones produce UTC instants while retaining source calendar date/time; unspecified time zones remain unspecified. USGS daily data remain source-calendar-date daily means. Qualified or provisional results require a saved inclusion review; quality-control samples, unknown units and source-derived values remain excluded from usable inputs. Source revisions must be selected explicitly.

`upper-savannah-calibration-input` version 1 contains `accepted`, `excluded`, `counts`, `workspaceRevision`, source references and rules. These are measured inputs for downstream calibration and temporal matching. **Native annual loads PO4_KG/NH4_KG/NO3_KG, and native InVEST annual N/P or sediment outputs, are not concentration aliases.** This extension does not write them through `Workspace.import_observation_loads`.

`upper-savannah-paired-loads` version 1 calculates `C [mg/L] × Q [m³/s] × 86.4` as a kg/day estimate. The supporting concentration is a discrete sample, not a daily mean. Pairing requires an explicit chemistry station, discharge station and rationale; exactly one usable daily flow on the source calendar date; and preserves unpaired/ambiguous measurements. Censored concentration bounds produce load bounds, not point estimates. There is no interpolation, annualization or drainage-area scaling. Floating-point conversion is used, not an exact-decimal laboratory calculation.

snapshot = service.json("GET", "snapshot?" + urlencode(filters))
~~~

The response contains:

| Field | Native content |
|---|---|
| revision | Original nonnegative measured-data revision |
| total | Complete filtered record count |
| records | Full original record views in sampled-date descending, ID order |
| portable | Original upper-savannah-measurements/v1 workspace, including all source tables |
| summary | Original store summary plus the native reach list read for eligibility |

individual record read and this snapshot; there is one interpretation of these

paging. The optional expected_revision query parameter rejects a stale request

nonnegative safe integer. Pagination keys are rejected because this operation
returns the whole selected population.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Stream a complete Measurements directory into/out of a verified ZIP64 archive.

Invoked by the installed Node measurement engine, not a second scientific writer.
All hashes are computed from complete files. Existing destinations are never replaced.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
import shutil
import stat
import tempfile
import zipfile

CHUNK = 1024 * 1024
FORMAT = 'upper-savannah-measurements-files/v1'

def relative(name: str) -> str:
    if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or '\\' in name or '\0' in name:
        raise ValueError('Invalid archive member')
    if PurePosixPath(name).is_absolute() or any(x in {'', '.', '..'} for x in name.split('/')):
        raise ValueError('Archive member escapes its destination')
    return name

def digest(file: Path) -> dict:
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    size = 0
    with file.open('rb') as stream:
        for b in iter(lambda: stream.read(CHUNK), b''):
            h.update(b); size += len(b)
    return {'bytes': size, 'sha256': h.hexdigest()}

def pack(source: Path, output: Path, revision: int) -> dict:
    source = source.resolve(strict=True)
    output = output.absolute()
    if output.is_relative_to(source):
        raise ValueError('Place the archive outside its snapshot directory')
    if output.exists():
        raise FileExistsError(str(output))
    rows = []
    for file in sorted(source.rglob('*')):
        if file.is_symlink():
            raise ValueError('A complete workspace cannot contain a symlink')
        if file.is_file():
            name = relative(file.relative_to(source).as_posix())
            if name == 'MEASUREMENTS_ARCHIVE.json':
                raise ValueError('Reserved manifest name in workspace')
            rows.append({'path': name, **digest(file)})
        elif not file.is_dir():
            raise ValueError('A workspace member is not a regular file')
    if not any(x['path'] == 'measurements.sqlite' for x in rows):
        raise ValueError('Native measurement database is absent')
    manifest = {'format': FORMAT, 'revision': revision, 'files': rows}
    output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fd, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix='.measurements-', dir=output.parent)
    os.close(fd)
    temporary = Path(temporary)
    try:
        with zipfile.ZipFile(temporary, 'w', compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED,
                             compresslevel=6, allowZip64=True) as archive:
            for row in rows:
                archive.write(source / row['path'], row['path'])
                if digest(source / row['path']) != {k: row[k] for k in ('bytes', 'sha256')}:
                    raise ValueError('Snapshot member changed while archiving: ' + row['path'])
            archive.writestr('MEASUREMENTS_ARCHIVE.json', json.dumps(manifest, ensure_ascii=False,
                              sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')) + '\n')
        with temporary.open('rb') as stream:
            os.fsync(stream.fileno())
        os.link(temporary, output)
    finally:
        temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    return {'manifest': manifest, **digest(output)}

def unpack(archive_path: Path, destination: Path) -> dict:
    """A complete verified directory appears only after every original member passes."""
    destination = destination.absolute()
    if destination.exists():
        raise FileExistsError(str(destination))
    destination.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='.receive-measurements-', dir=destination.parent) as temp:
        temp = Path(temp)
        with zipfile.ZipFile(archive_path) as archive:
            infos = archive.infolist()
            names = [x.filename for x in infos]
            if len(names) != len(set(names)):
                raise ValueError('Duplicate archive member names')
            for info in infos:
                relative(info.filename)
                if info.flag_bits & 1 or stat.S_ISLNK(info.external_attr >> 16) or info.is_dir():
                    raise ValueError('Unsupported archive member type')
            m = archive.getinfo('MEASUREMENTS_ARCHIVE.json')
            if m.file_size > 32 * 1024 * 1024:
                raise ValueError('Workspace manifest exceeds 32 MiB')
            manifest = json.loads(archive.read(m))
            if manifest.get('format') != FORMAT or not isinstance(manifest.get('files'), list):
                raise ValueError('Unknown Measurements archive format')
            if type(manifest.get('revision')) is not int or manifest['revision'] < 0:
                raise ValueError('Invalid native revision')
            declared = [relative(x['path']) for x in manifest['files']]
            if len(declared) != len(set(declared)) or set(declared) | {'MEASUREMENTS_ARCHIVE.json'} != set(names):
                raise ValueError('Complete archive member inventory differs')
            if 'MEASUREMENTS_ARCHIVE.json' in declared or 'measurements.sqlite' not in declared:
                raise ValueError('Invalid native archive inventory')
            need = sum(x['bytes'] for x in manifest['files'] if type(x.get('bytes')) is int and x['bytes'] >= 0)
            if need > shutil.disk_usage(temp).free:
                raise OSError('Not enough disk space for the complete editable receiving copy')
            for row in manifest['files']:
                if type(row.get('bytes')) is not int or row['bytes'] < 0 or not isinstance(row.get('sha256'), str) or len(row['sha256']) != 64:
                    raise ValueError('Invalid original member metadata')
                info = archive.getinfo(row['path'])
                if info.file_size != row['bytes']:
                    raise ValueError('Original member length differs')
                file = temp / row['path']
                file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                h, n = hashlib.sha256(), 0
                with archive.open(info) as inp, file.open('xb') as out:
                    for b in iter(lambda: inp.read(CHUNK), b''):
                        n += len(b)
                        if n > row['bytes']:
                            raise ValueError('Expanded member exceeds its declared size')
                        out.write(b); h.update(b)
                    out.flush(); os.fsync(out.fileno())
                if n != row['bytes'] or h.hexdigest() != row['sha256']:
                    raise ValueError('Original member checksum differs: ' + row['path'])
            (temp / 'MEASUREMENTS_ARCHIVE.json').write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2) + '\n')
        # The engine checks source interpretation before admitting this retained copy.
        os.rename(temp, destination)
    return manifest

if __name__ == '__main__':
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest='operation', required=True)
    p = sub.add_parser('pack'); p.add_argument('source', type=Path); p.add_argument('output', type=Path); p.add_argument('--revision', type=int, required=True)
    p = sub.add_parser('unpack'); p.add_argument('archive', type=Path); p.add_argument('destination', type=Path)
    a = parser.parse_args()
    result = pack(a.source, a.output, a.revision) if a.operation == 'pack' else unpack(a.archive, a.destination)
    print(json.dumps(result, separators=(',', ':')))

"""Retain the native domain original for independently editable measured projects.

The outer Workspace remains authoritative. A received project's pinned original
is a fallback only after its native database has admitted that exact archive.
No file outside the measurement workspace is changed during receiving.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import sqlite3
import tempfile

FORMAT = 'upper-savannah-measured-domain-original/v1'


def _digest(path: Path) -> str:
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open('rb') as stream:
        for block in iter(lambda: stream.read(1024 * 1024), b''):
            digest.update(block)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def _inside(root: Path, relative: str) -> Path:
    if not isinstance(relative, str) or not relative or '\\' in relative:
        raise ValueError('Native domain source must be a relative original path')
    result = (root / relative).resolve(strict=True)
    if not result.is_relative_to(root.resolve()) or not result.is_file():
        raise ValueError('Native domain original is outside its retained workspace')
    return result


def capture_native_domain(workspace_root: Path, directory: Path) -> dict | None:
    """Capture the explicit original bound by the native operator before export."""
    directory = Path(directory).resolve()
    registry = directory / 'native-domain.json'
    if not registry.is_file():
        return None
    binding = json.loads(registry.read_text('utf-8'))
    source = (Path(workspace_root).resolve() / binding['source_path']).resolve()
    if (not source.is_relative_to(Path(workspace_root).resolve()) or
            not source.is_file() or _digest(source) != binding['source_sha256']):
        # A independently received binding may already carry its exact original.
        if retained_native_reaches(directory, binding) is not None:
            return json.loads((directory / 'portable-native-domain.json').read_text('utf-8'))
        raise ValueError('The selected native domain original changed; select its retained edition before exporting')
    target = directory / 'native-source-editions' / (binding['source_sha256'] + '.json')
    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if target.exists():
        if _digest(target) != binding['source_sha256']:
            raise ValueError('The retained native domain original differs')
    else:
        fd, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix='.domain-original-', dir=target.parent)
        try:
            with os.fdopen(fd, 'wb') as out, source.open('rb') as inp:
                for block in iter(lambda: inp.read(1024 * 1024), b''):
                    out.write(block)
                out.flush(); os.fsync(out.fileno())
            if _digest(Path(temporary)) != binding['source_sha256']:
                raise ValueError('Native domain original changed during capture')
            try:
                os.link(temporary, target)
            except FileExistsError:
                if _digest(target) != binding['source_sha256']:
                    raise ValueError('Concurrent native domain original differs')
        finally:
            Path(temporary).unlink(missing_ok=True)
    metadata = {'format': FORMAT, 'binding_sha256': _digest(registry),
                'source_sha256': binding['source_sha256'],
                'original_source_path': binding['source_path'],
                'retained_source_path': target.relative_to(directory).as_posix()}
    fd, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix='.portable-domain-', dir=directory)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as stream:
            json.dump(metadata, stream, ensure_ascii=False); stream.write('\n')
            stream.flush(); os.fsync(stream.fileno())
        os.replace(temporary, directory / 'portable-native-domain.json')
    finally:
        Path(temporary).unlink(missing_ok=True)
    return metadata


def retained_native_reaches(directory: Path, binding: dict) -> list[dict] | None:
    """Resolve a received, source-pinned domain, never a guessed external source."""
    directory = Path(directory).resolve()
    registry = directory / 'native-domain.json'
    metadata_file = directory / 'portable-native-domain.json'
    database = directory / 'measurements.sqlite'
    if not all(p.is_file() for p in (registry, metadata_file, database)):
        return None
    metadata = json.loads(metadata_file.read_text('utf-8'))
    binding_sha = _digest(registry)
    if (metadata.get('format') != FORMAT or metadata.get('binding_sha256') != binding_sha or
            metadata.get('source_sha256') != binding.get('source_sha256')):
        return None
    source = _inside(directory, metadata['retained_source_path'])
    if _digest(source) != binding['source_sha256']:
        raise ValueError('Received native domain original checksum differs')
    connection = sqlite3.connect(database.as_uri() + '?mode=ro', uri=True)
    try:
        if not connection.execute("SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='large_receives'").fetchone():
            return None
        admitted = any(any(f['path'] == 'native-domain.json' and f['sha256'] == binding_sha
                           for f in json.loads(row[0])['files'])
                       for row in connection.execute('SELECT manifest FROM large_receives'))
    finally:
        connection.close()
    if not admitted:
        return None
    # Re-evaluate the original explicit selectors. The IDs remain original strings.
    value = json.loads(source.read_text('utf-8'))
    def at(item, field):
        for part in field.split('.') if field else []:
            item = item[part]
        return item
    selected = at(value, binding.get('items_path', ''))
    if not isinstance(selected, list):
        raise ValueError('Received domain selection is not a list')
    ids = [at(item, binding.get('id_path', '')) for item in selected]
    if (any(not isinstance(identity, str) or not identity for identity in ids) or
            len(set(ids)) != len(ids) or ids != [row['id'] for row in binding['reaches']]):
        raise ValueError('Received native domain identifiers differ from their original')
    return binding['reaches']


if __name__ == '__main__':
    import argparse
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('workspace', type=Path); parser.add_argument('measurements', type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    print(json.dumps(capture_native_domain(args.workspace, args.measurements)))

# Measured records in Reach chemistry

Open **Measured observations → Bind reviewed measurements to Reach chemistry**.
This panel uses the saved measured-data workspace and the original Reach chemistry
case library in the same scientific project. A saved binding includes its complete
source population, accepted observations, exclusions, original source history and
an editable Chemistry child case.

## Select the actual population

Choose a saved physical case. Optional station, original source-date and normalized
parameter filters narrow the population before inspection. **Inspect original
records** reads the current measured revision, the full original rows, and the
selected case's actual reaches and species. It groups records by exact reported
characteristic, method and fraction.

A refreshed population retains compatible working mappings but adopts the newly
inspected measured revision. Review the displayed population before saving.
The native producer checks that revision again during preparation; changes in
source review or selected record versions require a new inspection.

The existing Measurements tab remains the place to review an original result,
choose a source revision, or exclude a record. Its raw row, retrieval sources,
laboratory/method, qualifier, unit, fraction and review history remain available
in this panel's individual record details.

## Define the scientific relationship

Complete the binding title, reviewer and explanation of why the measured population
supports the selected physical case.

For each station being used, choose an original native reach and record both the
assignment rationale and its source reference. The panel leaves assignments blank
until selected. Geographic proximity, a station label and a watershed identifier
do not establish a model reach relationship.

For each exact characteristic/method/fraction group being used:

1. Enable the mapping and select its measured quantity.
2. Choose the exact conserved mass basis of the modeled pools.
3. Enter positive weights for the species that form this measurement. Leave unused
   pools blank. Every component must use the declared basis.
4. Cite the source establishing the reported mass basis and fraction, then explain
   why the chosen operator represents it.
5. Enter a positive observation error scale in mg of the declared basis per litre,
   with its uncertainty rationale.

Weights define the observation operator; they do not convert a reported chemical
mass into elemental mass. The native binding checks explicit mappings and source
support. A total-nitrogen definition must use nonoverlapping pools: ammonia already
contained in TKN must not be added a second time.

## Time, censoring and roles

Choose either a source-supported model day zero as an ISO timestamp with an
explicit timezone, or reviewed explicit model days on individual records. A supplied
origin must include Z or an explicit offset such as -05:00. When using only explicit
record days, leave the calendar origin blank. Records without a usable timing
choice remain excluded by the native producer. The model's calendar origin is a
scientific choice; it is not filled from an arbitrary import clock.

Choose the default fit or holdout role and, if appropriate, a source date from which
records are held out. Individual record details can override the role or set a
nonnegative model day with its rationale. Use **Keep record timing and role** to
retain that individual choice in the working definition.

Supported censored observations retain their actual source bounds. They are never
replaced by a midpoint. Optional interval overrides use the native shape:

~~~json
{
  "original-record-id": {
    "lower_mg_l": 0,
    "upper_mg_l": 0.02,
    "lower_closed": true,
    "upper_closed": false,
    "reason": "State the source-supported interpretation."
  }
}
~~~

The numbers above illustrate the shape only; enter the actual record's values.
An override must preserve the original declared bounds. A reviewed left-censored
concentration may use physical zero as its lower limit. A missing finite upper
bound for a right-censored result cannot be invented.

Optional derived total nitrogen uses:

~~~json
{
  "measurement": "total_nitrogen",
  "basis": "N",
  "basis_reference": "Original source establishing elemental N and fraction",
  "basis_reason": "Why the selected native pools represent this measured total",
  "components": [],
  "sigma_mg_l": null,
  "uncertainty_reason": "The scientifically chosen error scale"
}
~~~

Fill the actual same-basis components and positive error scale. The producer uses
the existing STOICH activity matching and concentration arithmetic to pair original
TKN and nitrate-plus-nitrite records within the same actual activity/context.
When it creates a total, those component targets are removed from the inference
population so the sum and its parts are not treated as independent observations.
Every original component record remains in retained source material. Unpaired,
unmapped or unsupported records remain visible with their exclusion reasons.

The native request editor accepts the original Chemistry request schema. It begins

# Loads from a saved daily-flow study

`runFlowStudyLoads(study, contract)` in `measurement_workspace/engine/flow_loads.mjs` calculates an optional load product from the same saved Measurements study. It does not save a study, open a database, acquire data, change a source selection or match stations. The existing flow-workspace service owns persistence and export.

## Calling the bridge

```javascript
import {runFlowStudyLoads} from './flow_loads.mjs';
const loads = runFlowStudyLoads(savedFlowStudy, explicitLoadContract);
```

The return has `schema: "upstate.flow-study-loads/v1"`, unchanged `flow_study_id` and `flow_edition_id`, a `contract_sha256`, the kernel `integration`, existing-ingester `observationExports`, original `joined_rows`, complete `selected_flow_rows`, and `source_binding`. `observationExports` contains the context and admissible annual CSVs and metadata. The caller can retain them with the same saved study and export snapshot.

The complete kernel contract and unit, censoring, interpolation and coverage rules are documented in [OBSERVED_LOADS.md](OBSERVED_LOADS.md). The load contract uses an **exclusive** end date. The saved flow edition retains its original **inclusive** selected end date; the bridge admits a contract only within that selected calendar.

## Binding to the selected originals

The bridge checks the original study input SHA and every retained original response/sampling-source SHA. It uses the maintained flow normalizer to verify that the complete edition, including every ambiguous candidate, still follows that source selection. It verifies sample-date context with the original relations and samples, then calls the kernel's `retainJoinedRows` against the exact selected objects.

A different normalizer generation may have changed source-row identity. If a historical saved edition does not match the selected source generation, the bridge raises a clear error. Reopen it using its original producing source or explicitly create a successor through the normal flow-study route; do not relabel its old ID.

Every original candidate goes to the kernel. Ambiguous source-edition days therefore remain unquantified, even when the candidate values happen to agree. A missing flow day is retained in `selected_flow_rows`. No candidate is chosen by position.

The selected parent context owns each `sample_id`, including source-SHA:physical-CSV-row IDs. The full original sample object remains both in the original join and under `flow_study_original_sample` beside the mapped sample. Original sample IDs, times, methods, fractions, qualifiers and detection metadata are preserved.

## Spatial support cannot be promoted by a load contract

A contract must agree with the original station, gauge and relationship. Any claim of accepted support, matching location or matching catchment requires the saved relation to be exactly:

- `gauge_relation: "co_located"`;
- `flow_location_role: "matched_catchment_discharge"`.

Admitted support must retain the saved relation's source evidence. An explicitly recorded catchment ID must also match. Downstream-same-reach and upstream-reach relations with `regional_daily_context` stay context only. The bridge does not reinterpret proximity or network membership as coincident catchment support.

A contract can omit a station's support; its original concentration then remains context only under the kernel's normal rules. An unassigned relation cannot be replaced with a new gauge inside this bridge.

## Concentration mapping and source status

The initial adapter accepts the original derived nutrient fields: station/date, characteristic, sample fraction, value/unit, detection condition, limit value/unit, result status, qualifier, method ID and context. A canonical Measurements row without those explicit fields is rejected with the missing field names. Its generic numeric value cannot reliably supply a fraction, chemical basis, analytical method or censor direction. Such sources need a separately reviewed explicit mapping that preserves the original metadata.

The original USGS normalizer stores approval status separately from qualifier. Ordinary approved rows can have `approval_status: "Approved"`, `qualifier: ""` and `validity: []`. The joined contract explicitly uses:

```json
{
  "accepted_flow_approval_statuses": ["Approved"],
  "accepted_flow_qualifiers": [""],
  "accepted_flow_validity": [""]
}
```

The kernel's declared string conversion maps an empty validity array to the empty string. No `A` qualifier or `valid` label is fabricated. Other qualifiers, validity conditions and provisional values remain original and excluded unless an explicit contract accepts them.

# Measured concentration and discharge integration

This component extends the existing Upstate workbench's observation intake. It reads a selected complete daily-discharge edition and original concentration rows, retains their identity and qualifiers, and estimates mass only for explicitly matched spatial support. It does not acquire flow, choose between conflicting editions, infer a catchment, fit a trend, run InVEST, or turn unmatched concentrations into annual loads.

## Run the existing source preparation

Use Node 22.16 or later from the existing application:

```sh
node source_tools/prepare_observed_loads.mjs \
  --contract observed-load-contract.json \
  --samples nutrient-results.csv \
  --flows selected-daily-flow.json \
  --output NEW_OBSERVED_LOAD_PRODUCT
```

An optional `--joins sample-flow-joins.json` retains the parent's original sample-day join rows after checking their selected sample/date/station/flow identities. A matching sample day does not establish a matching catchment or fill unsampled discharge days. The original source files are copied exactly under `original/`. Every output is create-only, identical reentry is allowed, and manifest.json is written last. Keep sources and outputs separate. Open index.html; its links expose all original source rows, daily estimates, missing-day reasons and period coverage.

The pure engine `source_tools/observed_loads.cjs` is also callable as `integrate({contract,samples,flows})`. It has no filesystem or network dependency. The source CSV reader preserves quoted values, empty fields and original row content.

## Source contracts

Concentration rows use the existing nutrient-results.csv names: station_id, date, characteristic, sample_fraction, method_id, method_context, value, unit, detection_condition, limit_value, limit_unit, result_status, qualifier, source_file and source_row. A source sample_id can be supplied; otherwise source_file:source_row is the immutable row key. Dates are strict calendar dates. Original time/time_zone and other fields remain unchanged. The method groups never combine total/dissolved fractions, distinct constituents or analytical methods.

Discharge rows retain the existing usgs_flow.py ROW_FIELDS: observation_id, monitoring_location_id, time_series_id, date, water_year, source_value, source_unit, unit_source, discharge_m3_s, conversion_factor, approval_status, qualifier, last_modified and source_request_id. Additional edition_id/source_id/source_pointer/source_format/validity and original fields remain intact. The selected full daily series must already be reconciled. Two rows for the same gauge/date are unresolved even if their numbers agree: the component will not silently select an edition.

The contract is `upstate.observed-loads-contract/v1`. It declares period.start and period.end (exclusive), a positive maximum_interpolation_gap_days, and `daily_concentration_basis:"date_assigned_grab_with_daily_mean_flow"`. Explicit arrays name accepted concentration statuses/qualifiers, censoring conditions, flow approval statuses/qualifiers/validity. The event_sampling_policy is either retain_only or include_with_declared_bias. Samples marked event_sample remain outside interpolation under retain_only; unmarked source rows are not retrospectively classified as event samples.

Each station has exactly one support selection with original gauge_id, catchment_id, gauge_relation and original evidence references. accepted, location_match and catchment_match must each be true before mass integration. A downstream_same_reach label or upstream-network membership alone does not satisfy those conditions. source_references retain publisher/repository URLs. Seasonal intervals are explicit named subsets of the selected period. No season calendar is inferred.

## Calculation and coverage

Daily mass is concentration in mg/L × daily mean discharge in m³/s × 86.4, yielding kg/day. Concentration is linearly interpolated only between valid bracketing sample dates no further apart than the selected maximum. There is no endpoint extrapolation. The selected temporal approximation treats a date-assigned grab concentration as a daily concentration proxy; the product says so explicitly, preserves the original sample time and does not claim subdaily integration.

Quantified samples use their reported numeric values. Only the implemented original conditions Not Detected and Present Below Quantification Limit can be admitted as left censoring. A contract cannot reinterpret an above-limit, right-censored or unknown condition as a finite upper bound. Accepted left-censoring conditions use [0, reported limit] bounds in the original limit unit, with no fabricated midpoint or zero point estimate. These bounds propagate linearly into daily and period mass bounds. They are conditional censoring envelopes, not statistical confidence intervals. Other detection conditions stay unquantified. An invalid sample, unaccepted qualifier or conflicting same-day result blocks interpolation through that bracket. Identical same-day quantified values retain all their source row IDs. Event-sampling bias, unobserved peaks, flow error, laboratory uncertainty and temporal aliasing remain unquantified and are stated in every summary.

Missing discharge is not zero. Zero discharge remains a quantified zero mass. Every period reports expected, quantified, censored, sampled and interpolated days and explicit missing reasons. Annual and seasonal rows report only sums over quantified days; they never scale partial coverage to a year. Calendar-year completeness includes leap days. A period partially overlapping a year is labeled as such.

## Existing workbench observation import

`concentration-context.csv` and its metadata preserve every original concentration row as receiving-water measurement context; no concentration becomes a model residual. `annual-loads.csv` is separately produced. It contains rows only when the calendar year is complete, every day has an uncensored point estimate, spatial support is accepted, and an explicit native_comparison_mappings entry binds the exact constituent/fraction/method series to an original total-species definition and evidence. TSS and turbidity are never mapped to total sediment. Kjeldahl nitrogen and nitrate-plus-nitrite are not individually total nitrogen.

Use the existing API after reviewing the original catchment binding:

```python
import json
from model.observations import ingest
context = ingest(ws, CONTEXT_CSV, json.load(open(CONTEXT_METADATA)))
# Use the same existing observation importer for annual-loads.csv only when it contains rows.
```

The unchanged public source function is `model.observations.ingest(ws, path, metadata)`. The importer preserves its original annual_mass_rate/species/coverage/physical-catchment checks. Annual rows are estimates derived from measurements and a declared interpolation method, not direct annual measurements or native model outputs.

## Actual retained Eighteenmile product

The executed V8 source course uses all 589 original nutrient rows and all 2,192 retained daily gauge values from 2020–2025. All 31 members in the original gauge source bank were independently byte/hash verified. The source records form 19 constituent/fraction/method series at four stations. All 181 below-quantification rows retain their original limits. Original network support identifies SV-233 downstream of the gauge on the same reach and the other three stations on distinct upstream reaches. None is declared coincident catchment/flow support, so the actual product emits 19 context-only series and zero annual mass comparison rows. That is an actual data result; no loads were fabricated to make the workflow appear complete. New explicitly matched station series can be processed through the same unchanged engine.

Thirteen focused dimensional/support executions cover a known mass sum, zero/missing flow, duplicate flow editions, conflicting chemistry, censor bounds, extrapolation, maximum gap, fractions, spatial support, event policy, complete/incomplete leap-year annual admission, and explicit refusal of right-censor inversion. These are method examples, not environmental observations. The exact engine also ran the retained 589/2,192 source inputs. Physical Node filesystem and browser operation remain the existing equipped recipient's continuation.

## Scientific sources

- USGS explanation of concentration × co-located discharge and linear interpolation: https://water.usgs.gov/nawqa/pnsp/pubs/wrir984222/methods.html
- USGS NWQN methods, including different estimation methods and their application limits: https://doi.org/10.3133/ofr20171120
- USGS LOADEST documentation on model specification, censoring and bias: https://water.usgs.gov/software/loadest/
- Actual retained concentration source: https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/main/opportunities/upstate_forever_2026/source/eighteenmile-stream-nutrients-20261013/derived/nutrient-results.csv

LOADEST and WRTDS are not implemented or claimed here. The bounded interpolation method is a transparent first integration option; its uncertainty paragraph explains what it does and does not quantify.

## Matching-volume flow-weighted concentration (v2)

Every selected, seasonal and calendar-period aggregate now retains `quantified_flow_volume_m3` and the point/lower/upper fields `flow_weighted_concentration_mg_l`, `flow_weighted_concentration_lower_mg_l`, `flow_weighted_concentration_upper_mg_l`. The exact conversion is **1000 × mass in kg / matching flow volume in m³**. Both sums use the identical quantified days; missing concentration or discharge days enter neither sum. The result is in mg/L and is distinct from an arithmetic average of grab samples.

A censored period keeps a null point estimate and its propagated lower/upper concentration bounds. These are censoring/interpolation envelopes, not confidence intervals. A zero-volume period has zero transported mass but all three concentration fields are null. Incomplete-period means describe only the retained quantified-day support and do not become full-period or annual observations. Annual mass export admission remains unchanged.

The complete HTML period table and period CSV show mass, matching volume, concentration and coverage together. The kernel result schema is `upstate.observed-load-integration/v2`; prior v1 source/results remain in the repository history and the originally published `outputs/` files are unchanged. Create a new output directory for the v2 CLI product. Saved flow-study callers must bind the kernel generation when retaining a calculated result, while preserving the original selected flow-study identity.

# WO11 — official Lake Hartwell 2026 observations

This continuation uses the existing Measurements source collection, SQLite import, report and portable reopening APIs. It adds source acquisition and preparation; it does not create measurements, annual loads, a new analytical engine or a new dashboard.

## Source and scientific meaning

The captured station is SCDES/WQP `21SC60WQ_WQX-RL-26024`, Lake Hartwell northeast of Broyles Recreation Area. The requested period is January 1–October 13, 2026. The four official CSVs were acquired and fully read back on October 13, 2026: one station, six activities, 132 distinct result IDs and 132 matching detection-limit rows. Actual sampling dates are January 21, February 12, March 11, April 14, June 1 and July 6. The requested end date does not imply observations after July 6. Native SQLite receiving and browser use remain a separate producing-host course.

- Station: https://www.waterqualitydata.us/provider/STORET/21SC60WQ_WQX/21SC60WQ_WQX-RL-26024/
- WQP services: https://www.waterqualitydata.us/webservices_documentation/
- Official USGS profile examples: https://water.code-pages.usgs.gov/dataRetrieval/reference/readWQPdata.html
- EPA August 2025 detection guidance: https://www.epa.gov/system/files/documents/2025-09/wqxdetectionlimitsbestpracticesguide_final.pdf

**Correction of an initial implementation diagnosis:** “Present Above Quantification Limit” is an over-detect/right-censored condition. It must not be automatically converted to a point measurement. The concrete fixes are recognizing below-reporting/below-detection conditions, pairing bounds with compatible original limit types, and not substituting an estimated numeric result for its laboratory threshold. Missing, contradictory or multiple applicable limits remain unresolved. Raw reported numbers, all limit rows, units and qualifiers remain retained.

The new mapping directive `_wqp_detection: wqp-detection-conditions/v2` is explicit and enters the resolved native mapping/import identity. Unpinned historical mappings use their original normalization so existing portable studies still reopen byte-for-byte. This source does not migrate or replace an accepted historical collection. A future deliberate reinterpretation of old source must create a separate reviewed import edition.

For the parent’s new USGS v1 intake, the separate explicit mapping `_usgs_daily: usgs-daily-source/v2` recognizes both published timeseries and approval field spellings. Conflicting simultaneously supplied aliases reject the source row. Unpinned historical USGS imports are unchanged.

## Explicit characteristic edition

Use both `_wqp_detection: wqp-detection-conditions/v2` and `_wqp_characteristics: wqp-characteristics/v1` for the separately prepared `characteristics-v1` collection. The additional directive pins a new mapping/import identity. Omitting it preserves the whole earlier detection-v2 preparation exactly, including all resolved mapping fields and original record objects.

The new module recognizes the 26 actual source labels without broadening model calibration eligibility. TKN and nitrate plus nitrite remain separate from total nitrogen. Chemical basis comes from the explicit source speciation or as-X unit; conflicting bases remain unmapped. No molecular-weight conversion occurs. Total phosphorus requires unfiltered/total fraction and explicit P basis. Hardness with no source chemical basis remains unspecified. Unambiguous metal names retain their elemental basis. BOD5 uses the source's explicit five-day name or APHA 5210-B context, not an arbitrary biochemical oxygen demand label.

MPN/100mL and CFU/100mL are distinct microbial quantities; NTU and FNU remain distinct turbidity scales. Micromhos/cm normalize one-to-one to microsiemens/cm without temperature correction. pH retains its own scale, and salinity in ppt is not treated as a mass concentration. Original method context/name, speciation, result/activity depth and reference, relative depth, time/temperature/weight bases are copied into the new canonical records, as well as the complete raw cells.

All 34 actual censored results remain left-censored observations with no point value; their compatible original thresholds are upper bounds. Two hardness records retain `chemical-basis-unspecified`. Every original winter clock says EDT and two salinity records say 36.79 ppt. These are source review questions: no clock, value or unit was silently corrected. Repeated observations retain their distinct result IDs and are not averaged.

Scientific source basis:

- EPA nutrient field semantics and speciation: https://www.epa.gov/sites/default/files/2017-06/documents/wqx_nutrient_best_practices_guide.pdf
- APHA 5210-B, five-day BOD: https://www.nemi.gov/methods/method_summary/5715/
- Conductivity units: https://archive.epa.gov/water/archive/web/html/vms59.html

## Original measured data now included

This source collection retains the exact six annual NWIS responses for USGS-02186702 (2020–2025), the complete 589-row Eighteenmile nutrient derivation, and three newly received original USGS OGC v1 responses for 2026. The 2026 daily body contains all 285 dates from January 1 through October 12, with original values, observation identities, approval states, qualifiers, geometry and provider metadata unchanged. All 285 are Provisional; July 31 and August 1 retain ESTIMATED.

The new daily body contains October 12, while the separately retrieved metadata ends October 11. Both observations are preserved. The original source receiving receipt records actual known acquisition facts and the separate provider body timestamps.

| Selected original period | Daily rows | Mean discharge (m³/s) | Volume over selected days (m³) |

# Receive the original 36-record Chemistry reference through Measurements

This course uses the original authored four-reach mathematical example already
retained in the selected scientific Workspace. It imports the exact 36 original
calibration observations, their Project and all original run artifacts into the
existing Measurements collection store. It then prepares the reviewed native
binding, runs the original Chemistry calibration, renders its scientific report,
exports the editable case, and reopens the complete measured source in a fresh
Workspace.

The selected records retain their authored numerical-reference labels. The
regional field population remains in its original collection. The new collection
uses a unique reference-station prefix and the binding selects exactly its 36
records.

## Place in the Upper Savannah demonstration

The primary RFP demonstration follows Bryce's 2026-10-13 owner brief: actual
Upper Savannah geographic and source shapes; a 30 m native grid; the upstream
contributing domain, South Carolina reporting mask and utility areas shown
explicitly; and clearly labeled, realistic simulated inputs for native NDR/SDR
baseline, restoration and matched-control comparisons. Preserve the annual
nitrogen/phosphorus outputs in kg/year and sediment in tonnes/year reaching
streams, editable sources and model settings, maps and exports, cold reopen,
and actual elapsed operation history. Tim retains scientific direction, review
and the client relationship. The selected 1,296 ha source-geometry scenario is
explicitly simulated. This 36-record authored numerical-reference course
complements that primary regional demonstration with source handling,
calibration, reporting and independent receiving through the same product.

## Install and run the complete current source

Use the complete native application with the merged Measurements binding,
atomic snapshot and collection-companion update. The scoped receiving bank

when the script is launched from its staging directory.

## Exact source and timing

The receiver reads each original run artifact through native file verification.
The source collection retains the unchanged artifact bytes and full original
case/run documents. Its CSV adds an explicit transport representation, preserving
the complete original observation JSON in every row.

The Measurements CSV format requires a calendar field. This authored example
only defines model days. Its carrier uses **2000-01-01T00:00:00Z plus the original
model day**, labeled in every raw row and the source origin as a transport
encoding. It makes no field sampling-date claim. The binding leaves calendar
origin blank and supplies every original model day through a reviewed explicit
day override. The receiver asserts exact native output model days.

Ammonium and nitrate retain their separate original nitrogen pools. Each
observation uses its own original species at weight one, original concentration,
original error scale, original fit/holdout role and exact model reach. The source
method is labeled as the original REACT12 numerical-method reference. The
engineering review explicitly includes this authored reference for the receiving
exercise; it does not declare a field measurement or site calibration.

## What the course produces

The maintained collection preview/receive API receives the complete source set.
The existing source review operation records the explicit inclusion decision for
each original reference row. Its one-transaction snapshot supplies the complete
original rows, provenance/history, portable measured workspace and revision to
the native binding producer.

The binding's complete collection editions and their original ZIPs are retained
as scientific Workspace source companions. The native Chemistry child case
therefore carries the original full source set through editable export.

The course then:

1. Checks all 36 bound values, component operators, nitrogen bases, error scales,
   model days and roles against the archived original request.
2. Runs the original native calibration with the same parameter definitions and
   checks convergence, fitted coefficients and all original predictions against
   the retained completed calibration. Parameter tolerances are relative
   `2e-5` / absolute `2e-7`; prediction tolerances are relative
   `3e-5` / absolute `3e-7`.
3. Creates the original Chemistry report source and uses the existing scientific
   composer to render the actual PDF, HTML, figures and data. All edition members
   are copied to the outgoing downloads directory.
4. Exports the source-bound case and completed run through the original editable
   Chemistry ZIP operation.
5. Opens that ZIP in a new independent Workspace, preserving the physical Project,
   original completed request and all native run artifacts.
6. Receives the full original portable Measurements workspace and every selected
   source collection ZIP into that independent copy. All original tables and
   source/review history are compared, and each edition member is verified before
   extraction.
7. Adopts the original binding source for the received case and reopens the saved
   local binding. The complete scientific request remains equal; only the
   expected receiving case/binding/source metadata is rebound. The original
   selection remains in received-from provenance. The completed received run
   retains its full original request unchanged.

The script records actual native calibration invocation time and total invocation
time. Reopening an already completed run is measured as reopening, rather than
presented as a fresh solve.

## Outputs and continuation

The course writes:

def require(condition, message):
    if not condition:
        raise ValueError(message)


def equal_number(actual, expected, label, *, rtol=2e-5, atol=2e-7):
    require(isinstance(actual, (int, float)) and not isinstance(actual, bool)
            and math.isfinite(actual) and math.isfinite(expected)
            and math.isclose(actual, expected, rel_tol=rtol, abs_tol=atol),
            label + " differs from the retained original numerical result")


def json_bytes(value):
    return (json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2, allow_nan=False) + "\n").encode("utf-8")


def input_member(path, raw, kind="companion", **extra):
    return {"path": path, "kind": kind, "label": path,
            "sha256": hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest(),
            "base64": base64.b64encode(raw).decode("ascii"), **extra}


def original_inputs(workspace, case_id, run_id):
    chemistry = Chemistry(workspace)
    case = chemistry.get_case(case_id)
    require(case["project"].get("provenance", {}).get("kind") == "constructed-reference",
            "Select the retained original authored numerical-method case")
    run = chemistry.get_run(run_id)
    require(run["case_id"] == case_id and run["state"] == "complete" and run["mode"] == "calibrate",
            "Select the completed original calibration of that authored case")
    directory = chemistry._verified_artifacts(run_id, run)
    request = read_json(directory / "artifacts/request.json")
    project = read_json(directory / "artifacts/project.json")
    result = read_json(directory / "artifacts/result.json")
    require(request == run["selection"]["request"] and project == case["project"]
            and Project(project).fingerprint == run["selection"]["project_sha256"],
            "Original archived Project/request differs from its native selection")
    observations = request["observations"]
    require(len(observations) == 36 and len({row["id"] for row in observations}) == 36,
            "Retain the original complete 36-record calibration population")
    require(sum(row.get("role", "fit") == "fit" for row in observations) == 28
            and sum(row.get("role") == "holdout" for row in observations) == 8,
            "Retain the original 28 fit and 8 holdout choices")
    parsed = Project(project)
    for row in observations:
        require(row.get("provenance", {}).get("kind") == "constructed-reference"
                and row.get("species") in SPECIES and row.get("qualifier", "equal") == "equal",
                "Retain each original authored single-pool point observation")
        require(parsed.species[row["species"]]["basis"] == "N"
                and math.isfinite(row["mg_l"]) and row["mg_l"] >= 0
                and math.isfinite(row["day"]) and row["day"] >= 0
                and math.isfinite(row["sigma_mg_l"]) and row["sigma_mg_l"] > 0,
                "Original values, model days, error scales or nitrogen basis differ")
    return chemistry, case, run, directory, request, result


def collection_input(case, run, directory, request):
    prefix = "react12-reference-" + run["id"][:16] + "-"
    columns = ("stationId", "stationName", "organization", "activityId", "resultId",
               "sampledDate", "sampledAt", "characteristic", "value", "unit", "fraction",
               "status", "medium", "activityType", "valueType", "method", "notes",
               "original_model_day", "original_sigma_mg_l", "original_role",
               "original_species", "original_observation_json")
    buffer = io.StringIO(newline="")
    writer = csv.DictWriter(buffer, fieldnames=columns, lineterminator="\n")
    writer.writeheader()
    origin = datetime(2000, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    for row in request["observations"]:
        date = origin + timedelta(days=row["day"])
        writer.writerow({
            "stationId": prefix + row["reach"],
            "stationName": "Authored reference position: " + row["reach"],
            "organization": "TokenJunkieLabs authored reference",
            "activityId": row["reach"] + "-day-" + str(row["day"]),
            "resultId": row["id"],
            "sampledDate": date.date().isoformat(),
            "sampledAt": date.isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z"),
            "characteristic": SPECIES[row["species"]]["characteristic"],
            "value": row["mg_l"], "unit": "mg/L as N", "fraction": FRACTION,
            "status": "Authored reference", "medium": "Water",
            "activityType": "Numerical-method reference", "valueType": "Reference concentration",
            "method": METHOD, "notes": CALENDAR + " " + row["provenance"]["reference"],
            "original_model_day": row["day"], "original_sigma_mg_l": row["sigma_mg_l"],
            "original_role": row.get("role", "fit"), "original_species": row["species"],
            "original_observation_json": json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False),
        })
    raw = buffer.getvalue().encode("utf-8")
    members = [
        input_member("reference-observations.csv", raw, "wqp",
                     origin={"type": "constructed-reference", "native_case_id": case["id"],
                             "native_run_id": run["id"], "calendar_encoding": CALENDAR}),
        input_member("original/case.json", json_bytes(case)),
        input_member("original/run.json", json_bytes(run)),
        input_member("REFERENCE.md", (
            "# Original authored numerical-method observations\n\n"
            "This collection retains all 36 original calibration observations with their "
            "exact values, species, model days, scales, roles and provenance. "
            "The CSV uses the original Measurements parser's column vocabulary; its origin "
            "is the retained REACT12 authored reference.\n\n" + CALENDAR + "\n\n"
            "Every native run artifact is included unchanged under original/run/.\n"
        ).encode("utf-8")),
    ]
    for item in run["artifacts"]:
        path = verify_file(directory, item)
        members.append(input_member("original/run/" + item["path"], path.read_bytes()))
    return {"format": "upper-savannah-measurement-collection/v1",
            "title": "Original REACT12 36-record authored reference", "files": members}, prefix


def original_rows(snapshot, original, prefix):
    expected = {row["id"]: row for row in original["observations"]}
    require(snapshot["total"] == len(snapshot["records"]) == 36,
            "The selected original reference population must have exactly 36 records")
    result = {}
    for row in snapshot["records"]:
        raw = row["raw"]
        native = expected.get(row["sourceResultId"])
        require(native is not None and row["id"] not in result,
                "A reference record is absent, duplicated or replaced")
        require(json.loads(raw["original_observation_json"]) == native
                and row["stationId"] == prefix + native["reach"]
                and row["value"] == native["mg_l"] and row["unit"] == "mg/L"
                and row["basis"] == "N" and row["censor"] == "none"
                and float(raw["original_model_day"]) == native["day"]
                and float(raw["original_sigma_mg_l"]) == native["sigma_mg_l"]
                and raw["original_role"] == native.get("role", "fit"),
                "Original value, model time, scale, role, pool or provenance changed in Measurements")
        result[row["id"]] = native
    require({value["id"] for value in result.values()} == set(expected),
            "The original 36-record reference inventory differs")
    return result
